summary: This sermon introduces a four-week series on service by arguing that genuine service flows naturally from receiving God's love and being spiritually formed into Christ's image, rather than from merely performing religious duties. The preacher challenges the congregation to measure their spiritual maturity by fruit (love, kindness, patience) rather than performance (rule-following, discipline consistency), emphasizing that spiritual formation exists not for personal benefit but to shape believers into partners with Christ in restoring the world.
key_points: Service is both a natural and intentional result of receiving God's love
Spiritual maturity should be measured by fruit, not performance or rule-following
Spiritual formation is for the benefit of others, not just ourselves—it shapes us to partner with Christ in restoring the world
How we treat others directly indicates our own receptiveness to God's love
Start serving in mundane, ordinary relationships with family and neighbors rather than seeking flashy volunteer opportunities
big_idea: True Christian service is not manufactured through performance or discipline but flows naturally from hearts transformed by God's love, manifesting first in ordinary relationships before extraordinary acts.
title: PTW Service: LOVE
